reference_observations.description: Supply recipes are historical text, not executable task instructions. Orders are not proof of delivery, use in a particular experiment or a common transaction. Public quotations and tentative explanations must not become unqualified Charles facts.

corrections.description: First-pass blanket outside-period claim is too strong for the six Baxter orders. Their bounds overlap the current period; they remain date/recipient holds, with no newly identified prompt.

The detailed ant report is Hague P4–16; Darwin introduction/signature is P2–3. Do not call all the experimental narrative Darwin own body. Publication April10 differs from before-April3 composition bound.
First pass says Hague confirmation is embedded. The preserved body contains only Darwin cover despite its Here follows wording; the complete confirmation is absent.
The brief signed and dated supply order is not shown to be a fragment merely by its F suffix. Original metadata calls it ALS.
Retain 474 exclusive monthly day-2 alternatives and the heading/XML endpoint discrepancy. Do not compress these to a chosen day or continuous composition span.
Authored day10 remains a constraint even though raw XML uses one broad interval rather than separate day10 alternatives.

summary: Sixteen targets reuse matched prior full primary readings. Ten public records have 1871–81 contexts; six Baxter supply orders have unresolved broad or alternative dates and cannot be simply declared later. No new links. Embedded Huggins, Nichols, Hague, Müller and Sanderson voices, missing confirmations, source arithmetic and author memory errors retain their scopes.
